key_big: Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Every digit you bring down needs a digit in the answer, even 0.
key_sub: 7,248 ÷ 24: 72 ÷ 24 = 3, 4 ÷ 24 = 0, 48 ÷ 24 = 2, so the answer is 302. A remainder is always less than the divisor. In word problems, decide: round up, round down, or write the remainder as a fraction or decimal.
body_html:
The big idea

Long division and short division both share a number into equal groups, one digit at a time, from the left. You divide, multiply, subtract and bring down the next digit. Short division does the subtracting in your head. Long division writes every step down, which helps with two-digit numbers.

Short division: the bus stop method

Write the number under the “bus stop” and the divisor outside. Divide each digit. If there is a remainder, write it as a small digit in front of the next digit.

Short division also works for easy two-digit numbers such as 11, 12, 15 and 25.

Long division by a two-digit number

First list some multiples of the divisor. Then each step is easy: find the largest multiple that fits.

SATs-style arithmetic

6,240 ÷ 24 = ?

62 ÷ 24 = 2, 62 − 48 = 14. Bring down 4: 144 ÷ 24 = 6, 144 − 144 = 0. Bring down 0: 24 does not go into 0, so write 0. Check: 260 × 24 = 6,240.

Answer: 260 (not 26)

Remainders: r, fraction or decimal

Write it asHow17 ÷ 4
a remainderWrite r and the whole number left over4 r 1
a fractionPut the remainder over the divisor, then simplify4 14
a decimalChange the fraction to a decimal (or keep dividing)4.25 (not 4.1)

Word problems: what does the remainder mean?

The question asksDo this500 people, 48 seats on each coach: 500 ÷ 48 = 10 r 20
How many are needed for everyone?Round up11 coaches
How many full groups?Round down10 full coaches
How many are left over?The remainder is the answer20 people
Sharing something that can be split (cake, money, length)Use a fraction or a decimal3 cakes ÷ 4 = 34 cake each

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a zero (6,240 ÷ 24 = 26)Every digit you bring down needs a digit in the answer, even 0: 260
A remainder bigger than the divisor (49 r 81 for ÷ 48)The divisor goes in once more: 50 r 33
Writing r 5 as .5 (39 r 5 = 39.5 for ÷ 8)r 5 means 58 = 0.625, so 39.625
Rounding the wrong way (10 coaches for 500 people)Ask: does everyone need a place? Then round up

faq.q: How do you do long division in Year 6?
faq.a: Divide, multiply, subtract and bring down the next digit, working from the left. For a two-digit divisor it helps to list its multiples first, then pick the largest one that fits at each step.

faq.q: What is the difference between short division and long division?
faq.a: Both work digit by digit. In short division (the bus stop method) you work out the subtraction in your head and write the remainder small; in long division you write every multiplication and subtraction underneath.

faq.q: How do you write a remainder as a fraction or a decimal?
faq.a: Put the remainder over the divisor and simplify: 17 ÷ 4 = 4 r 1 = 4 1/4. Then change the fraction to a decimal: 4 1/4 = 4.25.

faq.q: Is long division in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. The arithmetic paper usually asks pupils to divide a 3-digit or 4-digit number by a two-digit number, and the reasoning papers include word problems where the remainder must be interpreted.

items.e: 1 ÷ 25: 25 does not go into 1, so carry the 1 to make 19; 19 ÷ 25: 25 does not go into 19, so carry the 19 to make 194; 194 ÷ 25 = 7 r 19, carry the 19 to make 193; 193 ÷ 25 = 7 r 18. Answer: 77 r 18. Check: 77 × 25 + 18 = 1,943.

items.q: You use long division for 800 ÷ 13. The first step is 80 ÷ 13. Which multiple of 13 do you subtract from 80?
items.e: List the multiples of 13: 13, 26, 39, 52, 65, … The largest one that is not more than 80 is 6 × 13 = 78. 80 − 78 = 2. Then bring down the next digit. The whole answer: 800 ÷ 13 = 61 r 7.

items.q: What is the remainder when 892 is divided by 35?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the answer to the division. 8 is less than 35, so start with 89. 89 ÷ 35 = 2: 2 × 35 = 70, 89 − 70 = 19. Bring down 2 to make 192: 192 ÷ 35 = 5: 5 × 35 = 175, 192 − 175 = 17. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 17. Answer: 25 r 17. Check: 25 × 35 + 17 = 892.

sets.title: Remainders as whole numbers, fractions and decimals

items.q: Work out 1,644 ÷ 50. Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 1,644 ÷ 50 = 32 r 44. The remainder 44 out of 50 is 4450 = 44 ÷ 50 = 0.88. So the answer is 32.88, not 32.44.

items.q: Work out 4,676 ÷ 25. Give your answer as a decimal.

items.q: Work out 3,086 ÷ 24. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 3,086 ÷ 24 = 128 r 14, and 3,086 ÷ 24 = 128.583… (keep dividing: add a decimal point and zeros). The hundredths digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so round the tenths up: 128.6.

items.q: Work out 3,115 ÷ 29. Give your answer as a mixed number.

items.q: Work out 604 ÷ 38. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

sets.title: Word problems: what to do with the remainder

items.q: Ethan shares 395 stickers equally among 24 pupils. Each pupil gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 24, so start with 39. 39 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 39 − 24 = 15. Bring down 5 to make 155: 155 ÷ 24 = 6: 6 × 24 = 144, 155 − 144 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. So 395 ÷ 24 = 16 r 11. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 11 stickers.

items.q: A school orders 3,384 pencils. They come in packs of 24. How many packs does the school order?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 24, so start with 33. 33 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 33 − 24 = 9. Bring down 8 to make 98: 98 ÷ 24 = 4: 4 × 24 = 96, 98 − 96 = 2. Bring down 4 to make 24: 24 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 24 − 24 = 0. So 3,384 ÷ 24 = 141. There is no remainder, so the answer is 141 packs.

items.q: A school has £394 to spend on footballs. Each football costs £16. How many footballs can the school buy?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 16, so start with 39. 39 ÷ 16 = 2: 2 × 16 = 32, 39 − 32 = 7. Bring down 4 to make 74: 74 ÷ 16 = 4: 4 × 16 = 64, 74 − 64 = 10. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 10. So 394 ÷ 16 = 24 r 10. The 10 pounds left over are not enough to buy another football, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 24 footballs.

items.q: A farm collected 1,247 eggs. It packs them in boxes of 12. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 12, so start with 12. 12 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 12 − 12 = 0. Bring down 4 to make 4: 12 does not go into 4, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 7 to make 47: 47 ÷ 12 = 3: 3 × 12 = 36, 47 − 36 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. So 1,247 ÷ 12 = 103 r 11. The 11 eggs left over are not enough to fill another box, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 103 boxes.

items.q: 72 bars of chocolate are shared equally between 21 pupils. How many bars does each pupil get?
items.e: Divide: 7 is less than 21, so start with 72. 72 ÷ 21 = 3: 3 × 21 = 63, 72 − 63 = 9. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 9. So 72 ÷ 21 = 3 r 9. The remainder can be shared too: 9 bars ÷ 21 = 921 bar. Simplify: 921 = 37. Each gets 3 37 bars.

items.q: Kai has a roll of ribbon 529 cm long. He cuts it into pieces that are each 35 cm long. How many full pieces can he cut?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 35, so start with 52. 52 ÷ 35 = 1: 1 × 35 = 35, 52 − 35 = 17. Bring down 9 to make 179: 179 ÷ 35 = 5: 5 × 35 = 175, 179 − 175 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 529 ÷ 35 = 15 r 4. The 4 centimetres left over are not enough to cut another piece, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 15 pieces.

items.q: A rope is 1,572 cm long. It is cut into 16 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: Divide: 15 is less than 16, so start with 157. 157 ÷ 16 = 9: 9 × 16 = 144, 157 − 144 = 13. Bring down 2 to make 132: 132 ÷ 16 = 8: 8 × 16 = 128, 132 − 128 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 1,572 ÷ 16 = 98 r 4. Lengths can be split into parts, so write the remainder as a decimal: 416 = 4 ÷ 16 = 0.25. Each piece is 98.25 cm, not 98.4 cm.

items.q: There are 269 people coming to a summer fair lunch. Each table seats 16 people. How many tables are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 16, so start with 26. 26 ÷ 16 = 1: 1 × 16 = 16, 26 − 16 = 10. Bring down 9 to make 109: 109 ÷ 16 = 6: 6 × 16 = 96, 109 − 96 = 13. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 13. So 269 ÷ 16 = 16 r 13. 16 tables are not enough: 13 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 17 tables.

items.q: 12 friends share a holiday cottage that costs £939. They each pay the same amount. How much does each person pay?
items.e: Divide: 9 is less than 12, so start with 93. 93 ÷ 12 = 7: 7 × 12 = 84, 93 − 84 = 9. Bring down 9 to make 99: 99 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 99 − 96 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 939 ÷ 12 = 78 r 3. Money can be shared into pence, so write the remainder as a decimal: £3 ÷ 12 = £0.25. Each share is £78.25.

items.q: A pizza restaurant shares 86 pizzas equally between 18 children at a party. How much pizza does each child get?
items.e: Divide: 8 is less than 18, so start with 86. 86 ÷ 18 = 4: 4 × 18 = 72, 86 − 72 = 14. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 14. So 86 ÷ 18 = 4 r 14. The remainder can be shared too: 14 pizzas ÷ 18 = 1418 pizza. Simplify: 1418 = 79. Each gets 4 79 pizzas.

items.q: Leo is putting 583 photos into an album. Each page holds 12 photos. How many pages does he need?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 12, so start with 58. 58 ÷ 12 = 4: 4 × 12 = 48, 58 − 48 = 10. Bring down 3 to make 103: 103 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 103 − 96 = 7. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 7. So 583 ÷ 12 = 48 r 7. 48 pages are not enough: 7 photos would still need a page. You need 1 more, so the answer is 49 pages.

items.q: A factory has 3,728 biscuits. It puts 28 biscuits in each packet. How many full packets can it make?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 28, so start with 37. 37 ÷ 28 = 1: 1 × 28 = 28, 37 − 28 = 9. Bring down 2 to make 92: 92 ÷ 28 = 3: 3 × 28 = 84, 92 − 84 = 8. Bring down 8 to make 88: 88 ÷ 28 = 3: 3 × 28 = 84, 88 − 84 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 3,728 ÷ 28 = 133 r 4. The 4 biscuits left over are not enough to fill another packet, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 133 packets.

items.q: A garden centre has 1,548 bulbs. It packs them in bags of 48 and fills as many bags as it can. How many bulbs are not in a bag?
items.e: Divide: 15 is less than 48, so start with 154. 154 ÷ 48 = 3: 3 × 48 = 144, 154 − 144 = 10. Bring down 8 to make 108: 108 ÷ 48 = 2: 2 × 48 = 96, 108 − 96 = 12. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 12. So 1,548 ÷ 48 = 32 r 12. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 12 bulbs.

items.q: Alfie bakes 46 cakes for a party. They are shared equally between 16 tables. How many cakes does each table get?
items.e: Divide: 4 is less than 16, so start with 46. 46 ÷ 16 = 2: 2 × 16 = 32, 46 − 32 = 14. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 14. So 46 ÷ 16 = 2 r 14. The remainder can be shared too: 14 cakes ÷ 16 = 1416 cake. Simplify: 1416 = 78. Each gets 2 78 cakes.

items.q: A school library is packing 1,741 books into boxes. Each box holds 32 books. How many boxes are needed for all the books?
items.e: Divide: 17 is less than 32, so start with 174. 174 ÷ 32 = 5: 5 × 32 = 160, 174 − 160 = 14. Bring down 1 to make 141: 141 ÷ 32 = 4: 4 × 32 = 128, 141 − 128 = 13. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 13. So 1,741 ÷ 32 = 54 r 13. 54 boxes are not enough: 13 books would still need a box. You need 1 more, so the answer is 55 boxes.

items.q: A school is taking 673 pupils and adults on a trip to the seaside. Each coach has 53 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: Divide: 6 is less than 53, so start with 67. 67 ÷ 53 = 1: 1 × 53 = 53, 67 − 53 = 14. Bring down 3 to make 143: 143 ÷ 53 = 2: 2 × 53 = 106, 143 − 106 = 37. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 37. So 673 ÷ 53 = 12 r 37. 12 coaches are not enough: 37 people would still need a seat. You need 1 more, so the answer is 13 coaches.

items.q: A ferry carries 26 cars on each crossing. 528 cars are waiting in the car park. How many crossings are needed to take every car?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 26, so start with 52. 52 ÷ 26 = 2: 2 × 26 = 52, 52 − 52 = 0. Bring down 8 to make 8: 26 does not go into 8, so write 0 in the answer. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 528 ÷ 26 = 20 r 8. 20 crossings are not enough: 8 cars would still be waiting. You need 1 more, so the answer is 21 crossings.

items.q: A train travels 1,428 km in 14 hours. It goes the same distance every hour. How far does it travel each hour?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 14, so start with 14. 14 ÷ 14 = 1: 1 × 14 = 14, 14 − 14 = 0. Bring down 2 to make 2: 14 does not go into 2, so write 0 in the answer. Bring down 8 to make 28: 28 ÷ 14 = 2: 2 × 14 = 28, 28 − 28 = 0. So 1,428 ÷ 14 = 102. There is no remainder, so the answer is 102 km.

items.q: A class raises £1,162 at a cake sale. The money is shared equally between 40 charities. How much does each charity get?
items.e: Divide: 11 is less than 40, so start with 116. 116 ÷ 40 = 2: 2 × 40 = 80, 116 − 80 = 36. Bring down 2 to make 362: 362 ÷ 40 = 9: 9 × 40 = 360, 362 − 360 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 1,162 ÷ 40 = 29 r 2. Money can be shared into pence, so write the remainder as a decimal: £2 ÷ 40 = £0.05. Each share is £29.05.

items.q: There are 233 children at a football tournament. Each team needs exactly 11 players. How many full teams can be made?
items.e: Divide: 2 is less than 11, so start with 23. 23 ÷ 11 = 2: 2 × 11 = 22, 23 − 22 = 1. Bring down 3 to make 13: 13 ÷ 11 = 1: 1 × 11 = 11, 13 − 11 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 233 ÷ 11 = 21 r 2. The 2 children left over are not enough to make another team, so ignore the remainder. The answer is 21 teams.
